bugs.summary: Assignment to data.frame column (`$<-` or `[[<-`) should convert POSIXlt to POSIXct
bugs.creator: BodeEmil

comments.creator: BodeEmil
comments.text:
When creating a new data.frame, any columns supplied as POSIXlt are automatically converted to POSIXct (unless they are provided "AsIS" with `I`)

However, I'd expect the same behaviour when adding or resetting entire new columns, with `$<-` or `[[<-`.

Consider the following example:
test <- data.frame(ts1=as.POSIXlt(runif(10, 1.4e9, 1.7e9), origin='1970-1-1'))
test$ts2 <- as.POSIXlt(runif(10, 1.4e9, 1.7e9), origin='1970-1-1')
lapply(test, class)

First we make a data.frame where we provide a POSIXlt-column, then set an additional second column giving exactly equivalent input. 
However, the resulting columns are of different classes, and this can lead to problems further downstream (for example, I encountered this when trying dplyr::sample_n, which complained my timestamp should be stored as POSIXct)

The example with as.POSIXlt may seem contrived, but e.g. strptime also returns a POSIXlt, and here it's more unexpected that classes don't behave consistently.

FWIW, I haven't included `[<-.data.frame` here. That fails in another way (it seems like it only takes the second-part of the POSIXlit), but at least it throws a (somewhat unclear) warning.

Environment info:
Using R 3.6.1 and 3.6.2 under Rstudio 1.2.5033 and 1.2.1335 under Windows 10 (all 64-bit)
Checked with R --vanilla via commandline for R 3.6.2 and R 3.5.3

comments.creator: gabembecker
comments.text:
I can confirm that this behavior remains in a recent R-devel.

This appears to be happening because `data.frame` converts its arguments to data.frames before combining them, which is where the conversion from `POSIXlt` to `POSIXct` is occuring.

```
> df <- as.data.frame(as.POSIXlt(runif(10, 1.4e9, 1.7e9), origin='1970-1-1'))
> lapply(df, class)
$`as.POSIXlt(runif(10, 1.4e+09, 1.7e+09), origin = "1970-1-1")`
[1] "POSIXct" "POSIXt" 
```

According to the documentation for `$<-.data.frame`:

> There is no ‘data.frame’ method for ‘$’, so ‘x$name’ uses the default method which treats ‘x’ as a list (with partial matching of column names if the match is unique, see ‘Extract’).  The replacement method (for ‘$’) checks ‘value’ for the correct number of rows, and replicates it if necessary. 

This matches the actual code for `$<-.data.frame` which strips the class off of `x`, checks the number of rows in `value`, reps `value` out as needed, assigns into `x` while it's still a list, then reapply's `x`'s class. 

Thus this is working as documented, at least. 

That said I'm sympathetic to wanting the behaviors to match. We don't have dual dispatch for S3 methods, so the only ways I can think of to implement this change (if desired) would be 

1. have `$<-.data.frame` convert `value` to a data.frame before shoving it into `x`, or 
2. hard-code a special case for value being `POSIXlt` to convert it to `POSIXct`.

Approach 1 seems *way* too fundamental a shift for this level of behavior change, and the amount of testing we'd need to do to make sure this didn't break anything else seems.. daunting to say the least.

Approach 2 is doable, if a bit hacky, if desired. Happy to prepare a patch, though I suspect if a member of R-core wants to put that change in it'd be easier for them to just do it themselves.

comments.creator: ht
comments.text:
For total consistency, I think `$<-.data.frame` would need to use `as.data.frame(x)` to convert back to a data frame rather than reapplying x's class to the intermediate list object.

However, you're right that this would be a major shift in behaviour. One particular case that would be affected is matrices/arrays. Currently a matrix is converted to separate columns by `data.frame`/`as.data.frame` but added as a single column by `$<-`/`[[<-`:

```
df <- data.frame(arr1 = matrix(1:10, 5, 2))
df$arr2 <- matrix(1:10, 5, 2)
lapply(df, class)
#> $arr1.1
#> [1] "integer"
#> 
#> $arr1.2
#> [1] "integer"
#> 
#> $arr2
#> [1] "matrix" "array"
```

This is well documented in `?data.frame` and I think there's a lot of code that relies on this behaviour in the wild. So I think Approach 1 is probably out.

I'm not sure about special-casing POSIXlt to coerce to POSIXct in `$<-`/`[[<-`. At the moment `$<-`/`[[<-` don't do any coercion when replacing a whole column. In some ways it would be better if `data.frame`/`as.data.frame` did not coerce POSIXlt in the first place, then users would be encouraged to explictly convert to POSIXct as required, leading to more understandable code. Such a change would  also have broad impact though and is not a decision we could take lightly.
